ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 6104, as amended) governs Yuhan Hoesa formation and corporate name; Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (FTRA, Act No. 18979, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree impose customer due diligence and beneficial-owner identification duties; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality requires verified real-name accounts; Financial Services Commission Regulation on Reporting of Suspicious Transactions and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act apply to cross-border app-store settlement; FATF Recommendations and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit guidance are binding supervisory standards.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy of the corporate registration record showing Yuhan Hoesa establishment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Registry Court under the Supreme Court of Korea (district court having jurisdiction over the registered office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille member use: Registry Court issue, then apply for Apostille at the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Hague member use: Registry Court issue, then obtain Korean MOFA authentication, then submit to the destination country's embassy/consulate in Korea for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are separate, parallel alternatives and are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Registration (with current registration status and no liquidation or restriction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Court for corporate status and National Tax Service for tax clearance certificate, as required by the requesting party
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille member use: issue the certificate, then apply for Apostille at the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Hague member use: issue the certificate, notarize if required, obtain Korean MOFA authentication, then submit to the destination country's embassy/consulate for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never used sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (for pre-incorporation bank account opening and representative appointment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial board of directors / founding members, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille member use: signed by directors, Korean notary public notarization, then Apostille at the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Hague member use: signed by directors, Korean notary public notarization, Korean MOFA authentication, then consular legalization at the destination country's embassy/consulate in Korea. The two paths are parallel and never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public (original) or Registry Court (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille member use: notarized Articles of Association, then Apostille at the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Hague member use: notarized Articles of Association, Korean MOFA authentication, then consular legalization at the destination country's embassy/consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are never applied to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter including account history and reputation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank (e.g., Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, Hana Bank) after corporate account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille member use: bank letter with authorized signatory, notarized by a Korean notary public, then Apostille at the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Hague member use: bank letter, notary public, Korean MOFA authentication, then consular legalization at the destination country's embassy/consulate. The two authentication routes are strictly parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before registration, every director, shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), any indirect owner above 25%, and person with management control must be screened against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, U.S. BIS Denied Persons List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Korean Financial Services Commission and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions roster, Interpol Red Notices, and relevant adverse-media and PEP databases. For any PEP, enhanced due diligence is mandatory, including source of wealth, source of funds, corporate history, and continuous transaction monitoring. Screening shall be repeated within 24 hours before any funding round and continuously on automated tools for sanctions designations. Results must be documented and retained in a compliance file for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (I-Registration; www.iros.go.kr) and the Korean Commercial Registry Name Search portal under the National Court Administration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Commercial Act Article 19, the registered trade name must be in the Korean Hangul script. The core name must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul; a Roman-alphabet version may be used only as a secondary trade name after registration. The registered name must follow a four-tier structure: (i) distinctive core wordmark, (ii) industry or business-purpose descriptor, (iii) unique identifier including numeric, geographic, or founder name, and (iv) mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa for a limited liability company. The suffix must be the final part of the name, and no other entity may register a confusingly similar name with the same legal form and business purpose.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Jusik Hoesa (stock company suffix) for a Yuhan Hoesa
Yuhan Hoesa except as the mandatory final suffix
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry court rejects a requested trade name, the applicant may file an immediate appeal (Juggan Hanggo) with the competent registry court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The written appeal must be submitted to the original registry office within 14 days after service of the rejection order, must state the exact ground of rejection and the legal basis for registerability, and must attach the initial application, name search result, Articles of Association, and identification of the authorized person. The registry court reviews the appeal and may issue a corrective order; if the rejection is upheld, a re-appeal (Jae-Hanggo) may be filed with the Supreme Court within 14 days. In practice, the faster remedy is to amend the name with an additional distinguishing element and file a new clearance application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Korean Commercial Act requires an actual registered head office address in Korea. A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding mailbox is not acceptable for corporate registration with the registry court; the registered office must be a physical premise with land-use permission for office use. Local tax offices may visit and may reject the registration if the office is merely a post-office box. For the vertical micro-drama industry, banks and app-store payment aggregators such as Apple, Google Play, and Stripe require a physical address in Korea and in-person KYC; a standalone virtual address will likely be rejected for corporate bank account opening and for foreign exchange merchant registration. A full-service serviced office with reception, lease documentation, and physical presence may satisfy the substance test, but a pure virtual mailbox will fail.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Is there a visible company signboard accessible from the street? (2) Are accounting books, invoices, and employment paperwork available on-site during business hours? (3) Is any other company registered at the same address, suggesting mail-dropping? (4) Can the CEO or resident employee meet municipal tax inspectors on two hours' notice? (5) Are utility bills and internet subscription in the company name? Quantified risk for a newly formed micro-drama LLC during the first registration year: approximately 20-30% chance of an unannounced on-site inspection from the district tax office of the National Tax Service and 10-15% chance from the registration court or local government if mail-forwarding or multi-company co-location is detected. Risk reduces to below 10% after the first annual VAT and withholding filings are completed and the office demonstrates ongoing commercial activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, specifically Articles 287-2 through 287-74 governing the Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), Article 289 (contents governing company incorporation), Article 292 (articles of incorporation), Article 295 (application for company registration), and Article 296 (register of partners); read together with the Notary Public Act for certification of articles and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act where foreign members contribute capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office, Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, Republic of Korea, with administrative coordination through the Korea Court Administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa together with the Certificate of Corporate Seal Registration required under the Commercial Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korea does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Incorporation must state the precise contribution amount allocated to each member. Paid-in capital does not need to be held in a blocked escrow account. However, contributions made in kind must be examined by a court-appointed inspector unless an exemption applies under Article 287-15 of the Commercial Act. For a foreign-invested company, remittances from non-resident members should be received through a domestic foreign exchange bank and reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, but no escrow blockage is mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA. RESOLVED by the Board of Directors (the Board) of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea (the Company), acting under the Korean Commercial Act and the Company’s Articles of Incorporation, with a quorum present and voting, that: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The Board acknowledges receipt of the members’ capital subscription statement and ratifies the total subscribed capital, the amount subscribed by each member, the agreed payment date, and the valuation of any non-cash contribution. The Board directs the managing director to cause each contribution to be duly paid into the Company’s bank account and, where any contribution is made in kind, to obtain a court-appointed inspector’s report before filing for registration if required by law. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts at one or more banks lawfully operating in the Republic of Korea. The managing director and the chief financial officer are authorized to execute banking documents, deposit corporate funds, issue checks, sign wire transfer instructions, and register the corporate seal with each bank. The Board instructs the financial officer to ensure that all payment transactions associated with Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe settlement rails are routed exclusively through the Company’s corporate bank account for audit and tax trail integrity. 3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts and fixes the registered office of the Company at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The managing director is authorized to execute or amend the lease agreement, to file any address changes with the Court Registry Office and the National Tax Service, and to receive all government and judicial notices issued at that address. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints the following officers with immediate effect: managing director, chief financial officer, corporate seal administrator, personal information protection officer, and compliance officer for the Short-Drama Streaming Application. Each appointed officer shall exercise the powers and discretions required by Korean corporate law, including maintenance of the member register, preparation of financial statements, tax withholding compliance, and protection of user data under the Personal Information Protection Act. 5. GENERAL DELEGATION. The Board delegates to the managing director the final authority to execute all instruments, electronic filings, registration applications, and ancillary declarations necessary to complete incorporation, obtain the business registration certificate, and open employer and social insurance accounts, all to be used solely for corporate business. 6. EFFECTIVENESS. This resolution shall become effective immediately upon adoption; the secretary shall sign the minutes, affix the corporate seal, and place certified copies in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public engaged through the Korean Notarial Association, with preliminary name search conducted through the Court Registry Office online system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, setting forth the corporate name, business purpose covering the production and global distribution of vertical micro-dramas and the operation of a short-drama streaming application, the registered office address, total capital, each member’s contribution, the rights attached to each contribution, the appointed directors, and the limitations on liability. Each founding member must execute the instrument in person or by a duly authorized attorney-in-fact before a notary public. The notary verifies identity and legal capacity, validates the date of execution and, when applicable, attaches the court-appointed inspector’s report for non-cash contributions. Before notarization, a company name search should be completed to ensure the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Korean corporate name.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of each founding member (passport or alien registration card)
Power of attorney if a representative signs on behalf of a member
Court-appointed inspector’s report for non-cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification or raises a formal objection, correct the defective clauses and resubmit the revised Articles of Incorporation for a new notarial certification. If the name search identifies a conflicting entity, file an amended name selection before notarization and reperform the search. Any disagreement with the notary can be brought to the Korean Notarial Association through the professional conduct review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration with the Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry Office, Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa to the competent Court Registry Office together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, proof of capital contribution payment, the court-appointed inspector’s report when non-cash contributions exist, a member list disclosing each contribution amount, proof of the registered office lease or title, a corporate seal report, and a power of attorney if filed by a professional agent. The registry officer verifies the statutory contents of the Articles, checks the name against the corporate register, confirms the office is within the court’s territorial jurisdiction, and examines the regularity of capital payment. Upon acceptance, the registry enters the company in the commercial register, assigns the corporate registration number, and issues a certified extract of incorporation and the corporate seal registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa
Bank receipt or deposit certificate proving payment of contributions
Court-appointed inspector’s report for in-kind contributions
Lease agreement and landlord’s consent or certificate of ownership
Corporate seal report and seal specimen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary instruction, cure the stated omission within the statutory period, usually two weeks, and resubmit the amended registration package. If the application is rejected, an immediate appeal can be made under the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act. For simple defects, voluntarily re-verify the capital deposit and obtain a new bank certificate before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in South Korea authorized under the Banking Act and licensed for foreign exchange business, such as the corporate banking division of a major Korean bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the incorporation extract, open the main corporate account in the Company’s name. Present the certified company registration extract, corporate seal certificate, corporate seal, identification of the directors, the first board resolution, ultimate beneficial owner declaration, and expected transaction information. The bank performs customer due diligence under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information. For the micro-drama streaming application, the bank may require a business plan stating the expected payment volume from Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe. All subscribed capital must be deposited into this account. The bank will issue an account opening certificate used for tax registration and for merchant verification by digital payment processors.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and official company address proof
Expected transaction volume and business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional documents under anti-money laundering or know-your-customer rules, provide a complete ultimate beneficial ownership table, the source of funds, and a brief projection of streaming revenue. If the bank declines the application, apply to another licensed bank with a strengthened compliance file. If an unresolved adverse decision is made, mediation may be sought through the Financial Supervisory Service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea through the HomeTax online portal or the local district tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the business registration application with the National Tax Service within the statutory time limit after business commencement. Enter the company name, registered office address, corporate registration number, representative details, main business code for motion picture, video and television programme production and online distribution, and the sub-category for short-form video content. Upload the corporate registration extract, corporate seal certificate, lease agreement, landlord’s certificate of business place, Articles of Incorporation, and representative identification. The National Tax Service will issue the Business Registration Certificate for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, and electronic tax invoices. Confirm that the tax office correctly records the bank account for offsets and refunds and that the e-Tax system is activated for issuing electronic tax invoices to streaming-platform partners.
required_dossiers: Business registration application filed on HomeTax
Copy of lease agreement and landlord’s business-place consent
Corporate bank account details and account certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the classification code or requests proof of place of business, submit the landlord’s evidencing certificate and amend the code under the correct Korean Standard Industrial Classification. If a delayed registration penalty is assessed, pay the small penalty promptly and file a written objection with the National Tax Service, supported by the corporate registration extract and transaction schedule, or file a pre-assessment review if the notice has not become final.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Employer and Social Insurance Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Workers’ Compensation and Welfare Service through the integrated Four Insurances Business Startup portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company as an employer for the National Pension, National Health Insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance. Complete the online business startup filing by entering the corporate registration number, workplace location, business type, payroll basis, and responsible officer. Supply the bank account information for automatic monthly premium deductions and confirm whether any employees are actually engaged in content production, engineering, or distribution. If no employees are initially employed, file a zero-employee declaration to prevent incorrect premium notices. This registration is mandatory for the micro-drama streaming enterprise even if the business does not operate a physical factory, because production editors, platform engineers, and administrative staff must be protected under the Korean social insurance framework.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account for automatic debit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the social insurance institutions raise a discrepancy in wages, workplace address, or employee count, file an amended employer registration with the relevant institution and attach payroll registers. If penalty premiums are proposed, submit a written objection supported by internal payroll and corporate records; if rejected, request reconsideration through the Ministry of Health and Welfare or the Ministry of Employment and Labor as applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Seal Registration, and Digital-Content Compliance Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry Office for corporate seal registration; the Company’s board for governance minutes; the Personal Information Protection Commission and the Ministry of Science and ICT for digital-content review declarations where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the corporate governance opening file immediately after incorporation: register the corporate seal certificate with the Court Registry Office, execute the minutes of the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, keep the member register, maintain the capital contribution ledger, and store the official recorded address and seal certificate at the registered office. Conduct a compliance review of the short-drama streaming application under the Personal Information Protection Act, prepare privacy policies and terms of service, and assess whether content distribution over the internet requires any sectoral notification, although no physical operating license is required for pure digital production and distribution. The board must schedule the annual general meeting, authorize the preparation of Korean GAAP financial statements, and maintain a corporate record book for later tax filing and licensing stages.
required_dossiers: Member register and capital contribution ledger
Privacy policy draft and personal information handling checklist
Bank account and banking authorization records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate seal registration is delayed or rejected, correct the seal specimen and re-submit to the Court Registry Office. If statutory minutes or registers are incomplete, prepare corrected back-dated instruments and execute all required signatures and company seals. If the digital-content review reveals an obligation to file a value-added telecommunications service report or a content-promotion notification, effect that filing immediately through the designated ministry portal before commencing commercial streaming operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The entity is engaged in pure digital vertical micro-drama production and global streaming distribution under ISIC 5911; it does not operate a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility requiring an industrial licensing board or municipal industrial authority approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No industrial operating or manufacturing license is required for this pure digital content production and streaming operation. The company must nevertheless obtain a Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service for corporate tax and VAT administration, but that tax certificate is not an industrial operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. The Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea may be the general authority for EIA, but no EIA is applicable because the company maintains no physical installation, factory, warehouse, or discharge point in connection with digital micro-drama production and streaming.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. The operation is information and communication content production, not an activity listed under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; therefore no environmental registration or full EIA report is mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There is no wastewater discharge, VOC emission threshold, or hazardous-waste handling obligation generated by the digital micro-drama production and streaming application. Ordinary disposal of used office IT equipment remains subject to standard e-waste recycling obligations under the Resource Conservation and Recycling Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. A civil defense fire safety certification, structural load inspection, or workplace-safety operating permit is not required for a pure digital short-drama production and streaming company. The company’s leased commercial office space, if any, must continue to comply with ordinary fire safety requirements imposed on the building owner under the Building Act and the Firefighting and Rescue Act, and the company must apply general occupational health and safety rules for employees under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic registration, filing, payment and electronic tax invoice transmission are performed through the statutory HomeTax system at hometax.go.kr; customs export declarations are lodged through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must first determine whether it has a domestic place of business in Korea; if it does not, it must appoint a tax manager or statutory tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes before submitting the Business Registration Application to the local competent district tax office or through the HomeTax portal. The application must attach the foreign company certificate of incorporation, constituent documents, passport copies of directors or controlling shareholders, the tax representative designation letter, and proof of the Korean service address for any domestic branch. After validation, NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number which also serves as the VAT identification number. A non-resident supplier of offshore digital services with no Korean place of business may instead apply for Simplified VAT Registration for Foreign Suppliers of Electronic Services through HomeTax, disclosing its platform channels, payment methods, and estimated Korean turnover. Once registered by a Korean company, the HomeTax digital certificate must be used for quarterly VAT filing even if no taxable activity occurred in a quarter.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or pass-through classification for a Yuhan Hoesa; a Yuhan Hoesa is a resident corporation taxed at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act, while shareholders are separately taxed on dividends. The only relevant elective regime is the group consolidation system for wholly-owned resident subsidiaries under the Corporate Tax Act, which is an optional consolidated filing mechanism and not a pass-through election; hybrid mismatch adjustments are mandatory under the International Tax Adjustment Act and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a resident corporation such as the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, no monetary VAT registration threshold applies; registration is compulsory from the date of business commencement. For a non-resident supplier of offshore electronic or digital services to Korean consumers, simplified VAT registration is required only when annual Korean-taxable turnover exceeds KRW 100,000,000; however, if the business is also a Korean resident corporation for corporate tax purposes, Business Registration is mandatory regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: General taxpayers must issue an electronic tax invoice for every taxable supply to another business or to any person who requests one, and must transmit it to NTS through HomeTax within one day after issuance. The clearance architecture is API/XML based and near real-time with D+1 mandatory transmission; all electronic tax invoices carry a HomeTax digital signature and are validated against NTS systems, and post-transmission alteration is a criminal offence. For business-to-consumer transactions, the mandatory Cash Receipt Card system instantly reports cash receipts to NTS, and for online app-store distribution using Apple IAP, Google Play Billing or Stripe, the Korean seller must retain the payment gateway settlement reports, platform tax invoices, and transaction logs as source evidence. Foreign simplified VAT suppliers must also issue an electronic tax invoice for Korean business customers and transmit it through HomeTax under the same clearance rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the VAT Act for goods that are physically exported from Korea and for services supplied for use or enjoyment outside Korea to a non-resident. For the vertical micro-drama streaming business, the Korean company may claim the 0% export VAT rate if the end consumer is located outside Korea, the digital content is delivered through overseas platforms or application stores for access abroad, the subscription or in-app purchase is billed in foreign currency or via foreign settlement systems, and the foreign exchange is repatriated to Korea within the statutory period. For physical merchandise, the goods must pass Korean customs export clearance and be evidenced by an electronic export declaration. Zero-rating is not automatic for cross-border digital services unless the entity can prove the place of use is outside Korea through geolocation, app-store region, payment card country, contracts and platform sales reports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Electronic Export Declaration (Export Declaration Confirmation submitted via UNI-PASS)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill for physical goods consignments
Foreign Exchange Acquisition Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, equivalent to an inward remittance certificate, evidencing receipt of export proceeds
App Store or Google Play settlement statements and payment gateway reports showing foreign-currency payments repatriated to Korea for digital content
Contracts, IP address geolocation logs, subscriber account country data, and transaction records establishing that the digital micro-dramas were consumed by non-resident customers outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If NTS determines that the export was not actually completed, that the services were consumed in Korea, or that the foreign exchange proceeds were not repatriated within the 180-day deadline, the zero rating is retrospectively cancelled and standard VAT of 10% is assessed on the gross supply consideration from the original supply date. The taxpayer becomes liable for the overdue unpaid VAT plus statutory additional tax penalties ranging from 20% for negligent misdeclaration to 40% for fraudulent misdeclaration, along with daily default interest accruing until full settlement. The input VAT credits related to the transaction are also clawed back. Where fabricated export documentation or deliberate evasion is demonstrated, NTS is obliged to refer the matter to prosecution under the Act on the Punishment of Tax Evaders, which carries imprisonment for up to five years and fines up to KRW 50,000,000, with increased penalties for repeat offenders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, serves as the central monetary and foreign exchange authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a largely free-floating current account for goods, services, and ordinary trade settlement, while capital account instruments remain subject to declaratory or approval-based controls under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is convertible on a visible-transaction basis without a surrender obligation, but conversion and repatriation require a legitimate underlying economic transaction and must be filed through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Corporate profit remittance from a Yuhan Hoesa is permissible once annual statutory audits, tax filings (corporate income tax, local income tax), and shareholder resolution are completed; dividend remittance is classified as a current-account payment and enjoys automatic permission only if the foreign-invested company has properly notified FDI and submitted the end-of-use statement. Practical hurdles include documentary burdens from commercial banks, average processing windows of 2-5 business days, and strict anti-money laundering substantiation of shareholder source-of-funds. Non-resident capital injection above USD 30,000 must be reported; equity contributions above KRW 100 million may trigger foreign investment notification; transfer pricing documentation may also be requested. There is no central bank surrender of export proceeds, but all export receipts must be collected within statutory timelines and matched to customs declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Korean exporters are obliged to collect export proceeds within 18 months from the date of export declaration for general goods and services. No mandatory conversion of export foreign currency into KRW is imposed, provided the foreign currency is deposited with a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea. However, if proceeds are held as foreign currency deposits, the bank must report the receipt to the FEIS; exporters must maintain documentary evidence such as export declaration, bills of lading, invoices, and settlement receipts for at least five years. Late collection beyond the 18-month period requires a reasoned application to the bank for extension with proof of lawful cause such as trade dispute or collection trial.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI and Inward Capital Injection
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD Multi-Currency)
Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Operational Current Account with Trade Settlement Module

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for Korean KRW settlement. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Airwallex generally cannot provide KRW IBANs without a domestic partnership and are not recognized as designated foreign exchange banks for corporate FX payments in Korea. They may facilitate non-KRW collections from SaaS or IAP streaming channels but cannot serve as primary treasury clearing rails for KRW disbursements, payroll, VAT tax payments, or profit repatriation. Any fintech payment service provider must be registered with the Financial Services Commission under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and a pure offshore EMI is legally barred from servicing the domestic treasury of a Korean entity without a licensed Korean bank acting as the underlying clearing intermediary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In general, at least one authorized officer or statutory director with account-opening authority must appear in person at a domestic Tier-1 Korean bank branch to execute the signature card, ARS/OTP authentication, and compliance interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for a newly established Yuhan Hoesa corporate account unless the bank already has an established relationship. A power-of-attorney arrangement is possible only if the designated attorney appears physically with a notarized and apostilled power-of-attorney, a certified copy of the overseas corporate register, and the principal passport. Non-resident directors must present original passports; an Alien Registration Card is required for any resident foreign director who will be the named signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient evidence of economic substance in the vertical micro-drama supply chain, including lack of operating history or prior content library ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Operation plan, content library ownership certificates, production and studio service contracts, monthly user cohorts and app-store analytics, international distribution agreements, consolidated trial balance, and 12 months of bank statements for the Korean legal entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA and CRS self-certification inconsistencies for the ultimate beneficial owner chain against the Korean shareholder registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Corporate Registry, Certificate of Foreign Investment Notification, original FATCA and CRS self-certifications for all ultimate shareholders, passports and proof-of-address documentation, share ledger, apostilled certificate of incumbency, and an explanatory memorandum reconciling discrepancies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal pre-payment pattern to overseas influencers, production houses, or talent in high-risk jurisdictions before monetizable net revenue appears on the app payout statements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service agreements with deliverables and IP ownership, talent release forms, payment milestone schedules, due diligence files and adverse-media checks on counterparties, SWIFT remittance instructions carrying explicit purpose codes, and tax-residency certificates or FATCA status per beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Apple, Google Play, and Stripe net settlements lending themselves to commingling of global user funds with ambiguous integration to the Korean entity's revenue ledger.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly payout reconciliation from each platform, merchant ID reports, VAT and GST tax invoices, standard licensing precedent, anonymized end-user transaction logs, rolling revenue-sharing statements, and an audit confirmation letter from the payment aggregator demonstrating clean fund flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound shareholder loans or capital contributions into the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be routed by SWIFT MT103 using a foreign-exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment or shareholder loan under FEIS. Funds must be received into a designated foreign-exchange bank account. If the equity contribution exceeds KRW 100 million, an FDI notification must first be filed with the designated bank and reported to the Bank of Korea and FEIS before remittance. The bank will issue a Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation; a licensed Korean certified public accountant then prepares a capital verification report. The inward remittance cannot exceed the amount stated in the investment notification; any shortfall or excess greater than 20 percent requires an amended notification prior to further transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for content licensing, royalties, and production fees should be settled via SWIFT MT103 with MT202 COV for bundled multi-leg payments. Commercial letters of credit are unsuitable for intangible digital content, so documentary collections at D/P at sight or electronic payment instructions are used for contractual settlement. For recurring profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders, the Korean entity must execute MT103 together with applicable corporate income tax withholding receipts and pay the dividend remittance fee to the remitting bank. All KRW-clearing between the corporate treasury, tax office, and counterparties uses BOK-Wire+ for high-value settlement and a designated payment bank for low-value batches; every outbound foreign-currency payment is automatically reported to the FEIS through the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Short-dated FX forwards under a single transaction basis for genuine trade receivables and payables, with maturity not exceeding 12 months
Cross-currency swaps from KRW to USD or EUR for balance-sheet debt restructuring after obtaining FEIS documentation and bank credit approval

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in KRW are not freely available to Korean-resident entities; a licensed domestic bank may execute a NDF only as a hedge of an approved underlying foreign-currency exposure and must file a derivative transaction report to the Bank of Korea

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Self-Assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea - local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the December 31 fiscal year end; automatically extended to 30 April for companies required to attach externally audited financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing negligence surcharge of 20% of the tax payable (40% if the understatement is deliberate or unjustifiable); daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022% on unpaid corporate tax from the due date; continued non-filing for successive years can trigger administrative closure of the business registration and eventual judicial dissolution at the request of the tax authority or other interested parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Return on Corporate Income (local surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si/Gun/Gu local government tax office under the Local Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April following the December 31 fiscal year end, or one month after the extended corporate tax return due date when the central return is extended.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% for non-filing (40% for dishonest filing), late-payment arrears of 0.022% per day, local tax seizure and compulsory execution, and continued delinquency may support administrative closure of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Auditor Appointment and Audited Financial Statements (conditional on audit thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members' General Meeting; audited statements attached to the NTS corporate income tax return; where applicable, Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) external audit report system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the ordinary members' meeting held no later than 31 March for calendar-year entities, or by 30 April if using the external-audit filing extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For failure to appoint a statutory auditor or to file audited statements, the FSS may designate an auditor and impose monetary penalties under the Act on External Audit; the tax filing may be treated as incomplete, triggering tax negligence surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Approval at the Ordinary General Meeting of Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Members of the Yuhan Hoesa (no public registry filing unless a registered change occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal year end; for a December 31 year-end, by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or to submit financial statements is a Commercial Act breach exposing directors to administrative fines (up to KRW 5 million) and civil liability to members; unapproved financial statements may impair the validity of tax refund claims or carry-forward positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-Driven Court Registration Updates for Membership, Director, Registered Office and Security Interests (including UBO-relevant share transfers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District Court Registration Office (Corporate Registry) of the competent Korean court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any registered-item change (e.g., transfer of membership interests, change of directors or registered office). No separate annual filing is required if no change occurs.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration gives rise to court-imposed delay fines (KRW 20,000 to KRW 1 million depending on the registered capital), loss of good-faith reliance protection, and in egregious cases judicial dissolution or removal from the commercial registry for a formally dissolved entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory external audit by an independent Korean CPA firm is triggered if the Yuhan Hoesa exceeds any of these conditions at fiscal year-end: (i) total assets of at least KRW 12 billion; (ii) total assets of at least KRW 7 billion together with one or more qualitative triggers in the Enforcement Decree of the Act on External Audit, including debt-to-equity ratio above 200%, average employees of 300 or more, or prior-year audited status; (iii) status as a financial company, holding company, or government-invested company, regardless of size; or (iv) voluntary appointment by members or a statutory request by creditors/minority members under the Commercial Act. Below these thresholds, a micro-drama Yuhan Hoesa is not subject to a compulsory statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed or large-audited entities; small unlisted entities may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Korean GAAP) or the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Entities, with both frameworks consistent with the Act on External Audit and the Accounting Standards Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not impose a standalone annual UBO filing for a non-financial Yuhan Hoesa. Beneficial ownership is maintained on an event-driven, register-based system: any transfer of membership interests affecting the registered members must be reflected in the statutory register of members and, if it is a registered item, filed with the District Court Registration Office within 30 days. Financial-institution AML/KYC procedures independently verify beneficial owners for bank accounts and payment-rail settlements; for foreign direct investment or real-estate transactions, Korea requires beneficial-owner disclosure to the relevant authority at the transaction date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,800 per year for registered office and professional corporate secretarial agent in Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 35,000 per year when a compulsory audit is triggered; USD 0 for a micro LLC below the statutory audit threshold unless the members voluntarily request an audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (top marginal rate; progressive brackets from 9% to 24%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general patent box or broad-based tax holiday. Eligible incentives in the Republic of Korea include: (1) Reduction/Exemption of Corporate Tax for Foreign Investment under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (RSTA) - a 50% corporate tax reduction for 5 years for eligible high-tech foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones (FEZ); (2) R&D tax credit under Article 10 of RSTA - SMEs may claim a credit of up to 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure, including digital content technology development relevant to vertical micro-drama platforms; (3) Special tax deduction for job creation (Article 29-7 RSTA); (4) Tax credit for facility investment (Article 26 RSTA). For the micro-drama business, core production costs and distribution fees may be subject to ordinary deduction rules, but there is no reduced effective tax rate for ISIC 5911 absent a FEZ or foreign-investment designation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Statutory Form: 'Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement' / 법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) including supplementary schedules, filed with the National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system at www.hometax.go.kr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., for a December 31 fiscal year-end, filing due by March 31 of the following year). A one-month extension is available for the consolidated financial statement group with foreign subsidiaries; additional case-by-case extensions may be granted by the tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identity and Residency Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, national tax registration number, registered address, fiscal year, number of business sites, industry code (ISIC 5911 / NAICS 512110), and declaration of Korean corporate tax residency. A resident company is taxed on worldwide income; a non-resident company is taxed only on Korean-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate 'Resident' for the Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC. If the company is deemed a foreign corporation because its place of effective management is outside Korea, attach Form 103A and disclose foreign control. Any ambiguity in residency must be resolved before filing because the entire tax base, credits, and treaty entitlement depend on residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from business operations, including subscription receipts from short-drama streaming apps, in-app purchase commissions, advertising income, IP licensing, and global distribution fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Korean-source and foreign-source revenue as a resident company. Revenue from foreign app stores (Apple App Store, Google Play) should be recognized gross, with commissions shown separately as selling expenses if the company is the principal. If the company is merely an agent of a foreign affiliate, only the commission income is creditable revenue; contractual terms and economic substance test will govern recharacterization. Attach app store payout statements and make transfer pricing adjustments for intercompany distribution fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of Goods Sold and Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs (production costs of micro-dramas, talent fees, set costs, editing, sound design), platform commissions, cloud hosting, server fees, licensing amortization, advertising and marketing, administration expenses, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For payments to foreign non-resident content owners or performers, verify whether withholding tax obligations arise; deductible expenses are allowed only if they constitute arm's length remuneration and are properly evidenced by contracts and invoices. Expense items paid to a related party in a low-tax jurisdiction must be benchmarked under the arm's length principle; excessive royalty or management-fee deductions will trigger penal adjustments. All cross-border service fees should be supported by a Transfer Pricing Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Non-Operating Income and Non-Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains or losses, dividend income, gain or loss on disposal of fixed assets, insurance proceeds, donations, penalties, and other incidental gains/losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-currency payment settlement risks from global distribution in USD or other currencies must be recorded at the Book-to-Tax reconciliation. For interest expense paid to foreign shareholders, the thin capitalization Rule under Article 15-2 of the Corporate Income Tax Law limits deductibility to 3:1 debt-equity ratio (2:1 for financial institutions). Dividend income from foreign subsidiaries is eligible for an indirect foreign tax credit only if the holding percentage and holding period thresholds are met; keep foreign tax vouchers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Reconciliation to Taxable Income (Tax Base Computation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line-by-line reconciliation from accounting net income to taxable income: add back non-deductible expenses (e.g., entertainment exceeding statutory limits, donations exceeding ceilings, unethical fines); deduct non-taxable income (e.g., domestic dividend exemption); and adjust for deferred tax assets/liabilities and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border intercompany transactions must be reported on Schedule 6 (related-party transaction schedule). If the price paid or received between the Korean company and any foreign related company differs from the arm's length price, an NTS-initiated adjustment will be added to the taxable base. If the company voluntarily adjusts to the arm's length price before filing, it can avoid the 15% negligence penalty. Unreported foreign-source receipts from app store sales are a common source of underreported income leading to criminal fraud audits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Corporate Tax Rate Computation and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply progressive corporate income tax rates to the taxable income base: KRW 0 - 200 million: 9%; 200 million - 20 billion: 19%; 20 billion - 300 billion: 21%; above 300 billion: 24%. Add the 10% resident surtax on corporate tax thereafter (effectively 0.9% to 2.4%) resulting in a combined effective headline of 9.9% to 26.4% inclusive.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean tax code applies the rate based on annual taxable income, not gross revenue. Micro-drama companies with substantial profits from app store distribution should carefully verify the total taxable income bracket and include all foreign revenues to avoid misapplication of the lower 9% bracket. If the company is in an FEZ and qualifies for foreign-investment tax reduction, deduct the reduced amount in the Tax Reductions and Exemptions section, not in the rate computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax Credits, Exemptions, and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax-reduction and exemption amounts: SME IP exemption, R&D tax credits, job creation credits, FEZ incentives, and foreign tax credit for taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions on foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a foreign tax credit (FTC) calculation using the recomputed Korean corporate tax attributable to foreign-source income. FTC limitation = Korean tax on total taxable income x (foreign-source taxable income / worldwide taxable income). Unused FTC carryforward is allowed for 5 years, carryback not allowed. Royalties or withholding taxes imposed by source states on distribution or copyright licensing must be supported by local tax deduction certificates. Claims for treaty relief must be supported by a valid Tax Residency Certificate; otherwise the credit may be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Foreign Payments and Withholding Tax Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of payments made to non-residents during the fiscal year: dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, leasing fees, and technical service fees. Indicate the statutory withholding tax remitted to the NTS and the beneficial owner's country.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident withholding obligations apply under Article 156 of the Corporate Income Tax Law and the Local Tax Act. For each payment, file (1) Withholding Tax Report (Form Treasury 21) no later than the 10th day of the following month, (2) remit the 22% combined withholding tax (20% corporate income tax + 2% local resident surtax), unless a reduced treaty rate applies. To apply a treaty reduction, attach: (a) Non-resident's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent foreign tax authority; (b) Beneficial Ownership certificate (Form 140-A); (c) proof of no permanent establishment in Korea; (d) a statement of actual receipt and entitlement to the income. If the Korean company fails to withhold, the company (agent) is personally liable for the unwithheld tax, plus penalty interest, and the directors can be criminally prosecuted for fraudulent suppression of withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Final Tax Payable and Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of total corporate income tax, less advance tax instalments paid (semi-annual preliminary payments) and withholding credits; resultant balance payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a balance is payable, it must be paid by the statutory due date; otherwise, delinquency penalty of 0.022% per day applies. If refund is claimed, ensure the bank account is recorded on the HomeTax system and attach all supporting documentation that proves the refund claim (foreign tax credits, incentives). Cross-border restructuring and recharacterization by the NTS will extend the audit assessment period to 15 years for fraudulent distortion; make a cash-flow provision for any disputed assessments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: For failure to file by the due date: an additional tax of 20% of the final corporate tax is imposed (non-filing penalty). For underreporting actual taxable income: an additional tax of 10% of the underreported amount (or 40% if the underreporting arises from fraudulent false statements under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act). For failure to pay tax by the due date: 0.022% per day on the unpaid amount, computed from the day after the statutory deadline to the day of payment. If the unpaid tax remains outstanding, the NTS issues a demand; continued refusal triggers asset seizure, bank levy, card payment prohibition, and travel ban (blacklisting). Criminal violations under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may imprison the representative director for up to 3 years (or up to 5 years if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million or involves repeated false entry) plus a fine of up to three times the evaded tax. All penalties are subject to aggravated amounts if cross-border related-party transactions involve a tax-haven jurisdiction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% corporate withholding tax + 2% local resident surtax) on dividends paid by a Korean company to a non-resident corporate shareholder, unless a Double Tax Treaty ('DTA') reduces the rate. For countries with a DTA, the dividend withholding rate is typically 10% to 15%; for example, with the United States it is 15% in the absence of a Limitation on Benefits denial (or 10% if the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of the voting shares and subject to certain conditions).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a DTA reduction on dividends, interest, or royalties, the paying Korean company must obtain from the non-resident recipient before payment: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction, stating that the recipient is a resident of that jurisdiction and is entitled to treaty benefits; (2) a Beneficial Ownership Form (Form 140-A, or equivalent) confirming that the recipient is the true, exclusive, and ultimate owner of the income, has full rights to income, and is not a pass-through or conduit; (3) evidence that the recipient does not have a permanent establishment in Korea through which the income is connected; (4) if relevant, a Limitation on Benefits clause certification showing that the recipient meets the ownership and base-erosion tests. The withholding agent applies the reduced rate at source; if the full statutory rate was withheld, an application for a refund may be filed with the District Tax Office within the statutory refund period (generally 3 to 5 years). In all cases, the Korean NTS is entitled to apply the guidance in the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) if the treaty is a covered tax agreement, and may deny treaty relief where the principal purpose of the transaction was to obtain treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 22% (20% corporate income tax + 2% local surtax). Under a double tax treaty, royalty withholding is often reduced to 10% to 15% (e.g., 15% under the Korea-US treaty, 10% under the Korea-Japan treaty, 10% under the Korea-UK treaty in certain circumstances); interest withholding is commonly reduced to 10% to 15% (e.g., 10% for financial institutions; 15% for others under many treaties). Where the royalty is paid for the use of copyrights or for the distribution of micro-drama IP, the Korean payer must consider the OECD royalty definition: payments for the right to use a copyright or for the dissemination are taxable in Korea; payments for 'shrink-wrapped' software or for the sale of digital content may be treated as business profit and not subject to withholding if no permanent establishment exists. Dispute resolution for treaty-stripping cases requires a merger application for notification of international tax evidence; in absence of treaty relief the statutory 22% applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCIAA), Article 11, a Korean company must prepare and submit (upon NTS request) a Transfer Pricing Local File and Master File when the annual aggregate amount of related-party cross-border transactions (goods, services, IP royalties, interest, and financial transactions) with each foreign related party exceeds KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.6 million) for the fiscal year. If the total aggregate amount exceeds KRW 50 billion (approximately USD 38 million), a Master File must be prepared also for the multinational group; if any related-party transaction is with an entity in a designated tax haven jurisdiction, the documentation threshold is zero (i.e., mandatory documentation regardless of amount). The Korean entity must also file an Annual Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form (Schedule 6) and the 'International Transactions Information Statement' when any related-party transaction exceeds KRW 300 million (approximately USD 230,000).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Republic of Korea does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulation comparable to that in the UAE, but the Korean tax authorities robustly apply the substance-over-form doctrine, anti-fragmentation rules, beneficial ownership requirements, and the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) under Article 19 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. For a vertical micro-drama holding and distribution company, Korean-source income from the exploitation of IP will be recognized where Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are actually performed. If the Korean entity is merely a shell claiming treaty benefits or passing through app-store revenue to an offshore IP owner without real office, staff, contracts, and decision-making, the NTS will deny treaty relief and reattach Korean-source income to the Korean company; the directors would face personal liability for unpaid taxes. In addition, the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) provisions (Principal Purpose Test, PPT) operate to deny treaty benefits where obtaining the treaty benefit was one of the principal purposes of the arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Underreporting Foreign App-Store Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean micro-drama company reports only domestic subscription revenue to the NTS while concealing revenue received through Apple App Store, Google Play, or Stripe from overseas audiences. The company intentionally fails to reflect foreign exchange currency accounts and uses personal offshore bank accounts of directors to recognise streaming fees, thereby suppressing the taxable base and evading corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (Korea) and Article 66 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. An additional tax of up to 40% of the underreported tax is imposed, and the unpaid tax attracts daily delinquency penalties (0.022% per day). Criminal sentencing: up to 3 years imprisonment or a fine of not more than three times the evaded tax; if tax evaded exceeds KRW 300 million, imprisonment of up to 5 years and a possible fine of up to five times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the doctrine of piercing the corporate veil, the NTS may disregard the company's separate legal personality if the company is a mere alter ego of the directors, particularly where corporate formalities are nonexistent and assets are drained to offshore accounts. Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, surcharges and penalties; their personal assets can be seized. In criminal proceedings, the director is criminally liable with imprisonment; the NTS will also report the individual to the immigration authorities, resulting in a travel ban (blacklisting) and refusal of passport renewal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mis-Pricing of IP Royalties to Offshore Affiliate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity pays an excessive royalty stream to a foreign related company in a low-tax or tax-haven jurisdiction for the right to distribute micro-drama content, where the royalty rate is significantly above the arm's length price and no substantive research, development, or production activities are performed by the affiliate. The contract is designed to shift profit subject to Korean corporate income tax into a zero-tax entity, and the Korean company does not maintain a local file or disclose the transaction accurately.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 4 through 9 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCIAA) allow the NTS to recharacterise the transaction, compute the arm's length price, and assess additional corporate income tax plus the 10% (or 40% in fraudulent cases) understatement penalty. Interest penalties accrue at a rate of 0.022% per day. The agency may also fine the taxpayer for failure to submit transfer pricing documentation under Article 11; non-compliance fines are up to KRW 50 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false intercompany agreements or knowingly submit ineffective documentation are personally liable for the re-assessed corporate tax under the 'alter ego' doctrine; the NTS may issue a demand for payment against the individual. In criminal cases, the director may be convicted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for intentional omission of income or false accounting, with imprisonment up to 3 years. Additionally, if the mis-priced royalty was remitted out of Korea without withholding tax and without treaty relief, the director is personally liable as the withholding agent for the unpaid 22% withholding tax, and is subject to a travel ban until the tax is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Report Non-Resident Withholding Tax on Outbound Dividends, Interest and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean micro-drama company declares and pays dividends to a non-resident shareholder (or pays royalty, interest, or technical service fees to a foreign affiliate) without withholding the statutory 22% tax, and without obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate or beneficial ownership proof for any treaty reduction. The company neither files the monthly withholding tax return (Form 21) nor makes payment to the NTS, and attempts to deduct the gross amount as a business expense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 156 and Article 157 of the Corporate Income Tax Law, the withholding agent is personally liable for the unwithheld tax; the NTS is empowered to issue a demand covering the unpaid tax amount plus an additional charge of 10% of the unwithheld tax (if due to failure to withhold) or 20% if a false withholding return was filed. Delinquency penalties of 0.022% per day also apply. The corporate payment is deemed a 'prohibited deduction' and disallowed, triggering further corporate tax assessment. Fines for intentional failure to withhold may amount to 22% of the relevant income plus possible criminal sanctions under Article 13 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: a fine not exceeding three times the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable as statutory withholding agents if the company fails to withhold or to remit. Civil liability attaches to the director's personal estate, and the NTS may seize bank accounts, wage income, and real property. The director will also be subject to a blacklisting travel ban until the tax and penalties cleared. If the offence was committed fraudulently (false invoice, disguised beneficiary, prior concealment), criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, and the director is disqualified from serving as a director of any Korean company for a period set by the court. The corporate veil is pierced to the extent of the unpaid tax and any income diverted offshore, plus appropriate punitive restitution.
